title: CoverGo raises $6m Series B1 to scale AI insurance platform
summary:

Sector Updates
CoverGo, an AI-native InsurTech platform serving health, life and P&C insurers, has secured $6m in the first close of its Series B1 round to speed up worldwide uptake of its technology.
Betatron Venture Group (BVG) led the investment, which also drew backing from a mix of returning and new investors.
BVG focuses on B2B technology businesses that are reshaping long-established sectors such as insurance, and now sits alongside a group of international venture capital firms and strategic backers supporting the company. The latest round takes CoverGo’s total funding to more than $30m.
CoverGo plans to channel the capital into building out its AI-native insurance functionality and scaling its go-to-market efforts. The company aims to help insurers overhaul and eventually retire legacy core systems, while introducing AI agent-driven automation throughout their businesses.
Since closing its Series A in 2022, CoverGo has grown revenue tenfold and has also achieved EBITDA breakeven. It currently works with 25 institutional clients spread over 15 countries across the Americas, Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Among its customers are major insurance names including AXA, Bupa, Generali, Sun Life, Prudential, Blue Cross, MSIG and Marsh.
The company positions itself as one of the leading global AI insurance platforms, giving insurers a flexible, scalable and cost-efficient route to digital transformation. Its AI agents operate across the insurance value chain, and a rising number of insurers worldwide use the platform to digitise and automate work spanning omnichannel distribution, policy servicing and claims handling.
CoverGo CEO and founder Tomas Holub said, “Insurance companies realize more than ever that they need to modernize their core systems. CoverGo is uniquely positioned to accelerate their digital transformation and drive efficiencies across the insurance value chain.
“This funding will help us bring our AI-native platform to more insurance businesses globally and accelerate our vision of becoming the operating system powering the world’s most efficient insurers.”
Betatron Venture Group managing partner and CEO Matthias Knobloch said, “CoverGo combines deep insurance expertise with a next-generation platform that addresses the complexity of insurance transformation.
“Its client adoption, international reach, and progress toward profitable growth provide a strong foundation for its next stage of development. We are excited to support Tomas and the team as they scale the business and help insurers embed AI into their everyday operations.”

title: Avante targets rising insurance costs with $30m funding
summary: Seattle-based Avante has raised $30m in Series A funding to expand its AI-powered employee benefits platform internationally, as employers look for ways to manage rising health care costs and reduce administrative workloads. The round was led by Frist Cressey Ventures, with participation from new investors Sorenson Capital, Hearst Ventures and Morgan Stanley Next Level Fund, alongside existing backer FUSE. The latest investment brings Avante’s total funding to $40m. The company plans to use the proceeds to expand into international markets and develop its network of AI agents, which help benefits teams evaluate programmes, assess vendors and automate routine processes. Avante also intends to improve the personalised guidance available to employees, helping them identify and access relevant benefits. The funding comes as employers face mounting pressure to control health care expenditure. Large employers anticipate a median 9.2% increase in health care costs in 2027, placing additional strain on HR and benefits teams tasked with managing spending while maintaining employee support. Many organisations still rely on manual processes and outdated information to oversee benefits programmes, despite managing multiple providers, insurance plans and regulatory requirements across different markets. Avante’s platform uses AI agents to carry out benefits-related tasks, including reviewing vendor performance, preparing for contract renewals and identifying gaps in existing programmes. The technology can compare contracts with claims data, flag inconsistencies in plan documents and track important deadlines. Last week, Avante introduced Ava Agents in beta, enabling teams to delegate recurring tasks to AI agents that return completed work for review. Employees can also use the platform to ask questions about their coverage and available support, receiving personalised guidance around the clock without having to wait for assistance from HR. Since launching 18 months ago, Avante has secured more than 70 customer accounts. Bookings have increased almost fivefold year on year, while every customer eligible for renewal has renewed. The platform now supports more than 385,000 employees and their families. Among its customers, Samsung Semiconductor has reported a 66% increase in employees and dependants discovering and using existing mental health support. News Corp has used the platform’s workforce data to accelerate decision-making. Other customers include Real Chemistry and Zscaler. Avante has also established partnerships with benefits advisers Gallagher, OneDigital, Segal Benz, Howden and USI Insurance Services to extend its reach across the market. Rohan D’Souza, CEO and co-founder of Avante, said, “Benefits teams are responsible for one of the largest and most consequential investments their companies make, yet they’re still operating with outdated information, archaic spreadsheets, and technology built for another era. We’re combining purpose-built technology with real-time automation and years of benefits expertise across the AI stack, resulting in 100x leverage for the people whose decisions shape the health, financial security, and well-being of millions. Few areas of work touch people’s lives more directly, and benefits teams deserve technology built for the importance of what they do.” Senator Bill Frist, M.D., co-founder and managing partner of Frist Cressey Ventures, added, “As a physician, I saw again and again how hard it is for patients and their families to find their way through our health care system. Avante is harnessing AI to make that system easier to navigate, so employees get better care and employers get relief from costs that keep climbing. Its team brings rare depth in technology, health care and benefits, and has already earned the trust of leading employers. title: Global Relay closes compliance gaps in Google Workspace
summary: Global Relay has extended its range of Google Workspace connectors so that financial institutions can capture and retain electronic communications created across the Google platform in line with regulatory obligations. The expanded connectors move data from Google Drive, Chat, Calendar, Meet and Gmail into Global Relay Archive. The aim is to let banks, brokers and other financial firms use newer Workspace features while still satisfying rules such as SEC 17a-4 and FINRA Rule 4511, which govern how business records must be kept. The release frames the update around a tension many compliance teams now face. Financial professionals increasingly rely on AI-assisted tools in Gmail and Google Docs, along with collaborative spaces such as Google Chat and Google Meet, to speed up their work. Each new tool, however, generates fresh records that regulated firms remain obliged to preserve and make available to supervisors. Video calls are a particular focus. As staff hold more conversations with colleagues, clients and counterparties over video, those exchanges become part of the regulatory record. Under the Workspace integration, firms can send Google Meet recordings, transcripts and related metadata straight into Google Cloud Storage, from where Global Relay can archive them. This folds video meetings into the wider compliance and records-management set-up already in place. The connectors also gather the context around each communication. This includes file activity and version histories in Google Drive, recordings and transcripts from Google Meet, and conversations and shared files in Google Chat, all with their accompanying metadata. According to the company, the result is a fuller picture of business activity than message content alone would provide. Global Relay’s connectors convert data from a range of channels, including email, voice and enterprise collaboration platforms, into a single standardised format. This gives firms one consolidated view of their communications inside Global Relay Archive. Holding these records and their metadata together is intended to simplify search and eDiscovery, surface patterns, flag potential risks and support better decision-making. The company positions its centralised environment as purpose-built for the demands of regulated sectors, arguing that compliance teams should not be forced to reconcile fragmented records spread across separate systems. The company presents the update as evidence that firms need not choose between adopting new collaboration and AI tools and keeping a reliable, compliant account of their business dealings. title: Fronted raises €1.7M to simplify global hiring and business expansion
summary: Nordic HRtech startup Fronted has raised €1.7 million (NOK 18 million) in a seed funding round to support its international expansion and further develop its AI-powered platform for managing global employment operations. The round was led by Swedish investment firm Kaknäs Invest , with participation from Skagerak Capital . Existing investors, including Antler and Sondo Capital , also participated, alongside a group of new angel investors. International expansion often requires companies to navigate different employment regulations, payroll systems and compliance requirements. Businesses operating across multiple countries may need to work with several service providers, creating additional administrative complexity and costs. Founded by Marius Blaker Høgevold (CEO) and Hans Nyvold Kjellby (Chairman and CCO), Fronted aims to address these challenges through an integrated platform combining cross-border recruitment, Employer of Record (EOR) services and company entity setup and management. The platform is designed to help businesses manage international hiring and employment operations through a single provider. The company's technology automates administrative tasks such as payroll calculations, tax reconciliations and employment contract generation. By incorporating local labour regulations into its software, Fronted aims to reduce manual processes, improve pricing transparency and simplify compliance across different jurisdictions. Marius Blaker Høgevold, co-founder and CEO of Fronted, highlighted the challenges businesses face when expanding internationally, particularly the costs and complexities associated with existing service providers. We are building the invisible software layer that takes away the headache of cross-border administration, giving ambitious companies a trusted Nordic partner to scale globally with total transparency and ease, said Høgevold. The new funding will be used to support Fronted's commercial expansion, extend its operational infrastructure to 70 countries and further develop its AI-powered payroll engine.
